synthesis: The candidate proposes that the sign-colored real-axis fibers are propagated through branch-point fusions and the reported intertwining of zeta and zeta-prime curves to govern both where the zero-bearing curves Gamma_{k,j} turn and how the fundamental domains Omega_{k,j} meet.
source_support: Unit u02 defines the red/black encoding of negative/positive real-axis preimages and uses selected real-axis fibers to form strips; u03 applies color alternation to tail placement, real critical-point interlacing, and unit-disc preimages; u04 constructs proposed fundamental-domain boundaries from collisions of expanding circle preimages and separately reports imported intertwining and color-matching rules; u05 attempts to exclude a turn over x<0 by isolating a paired Hadamard factor along zeta(s_{k,j}(x))=x.
nonparaphrase_operation: A dependency audit across the four units separates three mechanisms that the candidate joins: sign-color adjacency on real-axis fibers, circle-preimage collisions at critical points as proposed sheet cuts, and paired-factor argument comparisons as a proposed turning obstruction. The audit shows that the latter two are not derived from a common color-transfer step in the supplied text.
limits: Unit u04 does not use color matching to determine the incidence or meeting pattern of the fundamental domains; it asserts the needed branch-point count and cut geometry from earlier work, while color matching is invoked separately for simplicity. Unit u05 does not derive its turning claim from color alternation or intertwined derivative curves, but from an unproved passage from local paired-factor dominance to argument control of the full product. Figures, degraded formulas, and imported simplicity, incidence, and intertwining results add further proof burdens.
quality_reason: Rejected because the candidate turns the coexistence of several geometric constructions into an unsupported causal story: no supplied parent establishes that half-axis colors are transferred through branch-point fusions and derivative-curve intertwining to control both turning and fundamental-sheet adjacency. A weaker observation that the units repeatedly compare target-plane loci with source-plane geometry would be source-grounded, but it would not preserve the claimed cross-unit mechanism.
